facts.text: The first industry in Tuxedo was the Augusta Forge at the Ramapo River falls, founded by Solomon Townsend in 1783 after the war.
Tuxedo’s name comes from a Lenape word meaning “round foot” or “Wolf Clan,” reflecting the area’s indigenous heritage.
The town encompasses the village of Tuxedo Park, a historic gated residential community developed in the 1880s on land originally acquired from the Algonquin tribe.
The Tuxedo train station on the Metro-North line opened in the 1880s, drawing affluent seasonal residents and hosting the popular Autumn Ball.
Tuxedo still houses three historic churches, a train station, a library, a post office, a school, and a hospital, all built in the 19th century.
It helped supply fuel for the wood‑fired Erie Railroad, which was built in 1841.
